messages.subject: Dummy coded endogenous variable
parts:
Hello everyone! 

Fairly new to the SEM world so please excuse me if this question is obvious to the rest of you. I am predicting how self racial identification changes overtime in an SEM path model. Is is possible to have my dummy variables as the endogenous outcome of interest? If so how would I model that? Below are the two approaches I am thinking make sense, but please let me know if you have a different method or if these are correct. For this example I have 6 race groups (white, black, latino, asian, other, and multi-racial) with multi-racial as my reference group. 

model1 = '
#regressions
asianW2 + blackW2 + whiteW2 + otherW2 + latinoW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1 + x3_W1
'
or should it be modeled....

model2 ='
#regressions
assianW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1 + x3_W1
blackW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1 + x3_W1
whiteW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1+ x3_W1
otherW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1 + x3_W1
latinoW2 ~ asianW1 + blackW1 + whiteW1 + otherW1 + latinoW1 + x2_W1 + x3_W1
'

I hope this question makes sense.

Also, my X2 and X3 variables are proportions (0.00-1.00) do I need to specify this information in the model at all or unit as a continuous variable? 

Any help would be appreciated. 

THANKS!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Dummy coded endogenous variable
parts: Is is possible to have my dummy variables as the endogenous outcome of interest?
If so how would I model that?

That isn't a lavaan question.  You might want to post that question to the more general forum SEMNET:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
Also, my X2 and X3 variables are proportions (0.00-1.00) do I need to specify this information in the model at all or unit as a continuous variable?

No, there are no distributional assumptions made about observed exogenous variables when fixed.x = TRUE.
